title: Scam alarm going off
body: If this app is geared towards people with ADHD why does it purposely hit the user with a subscription purchase seconds after setting up an account?? This seems predatory and It immediately turned me away!
author: NaIaGaGaA

title: Have to pay before you test
body: Free to download, input all your data, then you can’t even see the layout or how it will help you before you pay $30 a month or the full annual fee. You should at least be able to interact with the app and see if you are willing to invest in it. Thumbs down
author: Mandi Vance

title: Science backed marketing ploy to target those with ADHD
body:
Honestly, quite upsetting. Claiming to help those with ADHD but it actually just takes money from those who are struggling and need help. It’s just another AI. You can use any free service to get the same result (chat, copilot, Claude, Gemini)
Not only do you spend ages on the app prior to them asking for payment. So it almost feels like you need to see what it can do. I tried to work through the task management process explaining my task paralysis and it asks the same questions over and over. They also do not offer refunds.
author: SarahJade95

title: Waste of Money
body: Total gimmick. Absolutely no help at all. $50 less in my account with nothing to show for it. Siri is more helpful tbh. Scam. Avoid at all costs fellow ADHD peeps

body: Haven’t found this app useful for ADHD at all. It’s glitchy and you have to pay to use it, no free trial.

body: it’s so bad, read the other reviews, doesn’t work, waste of money
author: ilah the wish hater

title: Predatory Practices
body: At no point before the final screen did it mention this was a PAID only app, with no free trial. Before even demonstrating what the app is going to do for you, they are already trying to prey on the ADHD people with tendencies towards impulsivity to get you to BUY NOW! with an “80% offer for only 5 minutes!”. Even if this app did what it says it does, no one should ever support those kind of scummy tactics.
author: Juichikun

title: Unhelpful, misleading, waste of money
body: Do not buy. There’s literally nothing this app does that can’t be done with a free gpt. I tried to have it do timed sprints with me and it couldn’t even keep a timer and gaslit me that it was and I was just having time blindness lol.
author: Glbear18

title: Yeah no thanks
body: Proof that AI will never truly understand or assist neurodivergence! If you enjoy being a mouse on a wheel and being asked the same questions in varying ways knock yourself out! By far the dumbest application I’ve ever used!!!!
author: SerahAy

title: Subscription
body: Waste of time. Have to pay. This is not good for adhd people because if they don’t like it and forget about it they will also forget to cancel their subscription. Needs a free trial with notification everyday letting them know how much longer the free trial is and then once it has ended money shouldn’t be take straight away it should be confirmed beforehand incase they forget about it.

title: poor form
body: They ask you for $30 just for an ai bot. Don’t do it
author: YellowYella

title: Fake and phony
body: The app is only paid subscription and is just a chat ai that doesn’t even work. You type questions it just repeats the same pre written answer over and over again. Makes me think it’s not even ai ? Fake and BS money grab targeting neurodivergent people you sickos.
author: -greer-

title: Don’t even bother
body:
This app gives off very predatory vibes. There’s no option for even a short free trial to see if it’s useful or if the interface works for you. Instead, it throws a “5-minute countdown” sale in your face for an expensive annual subscription. That kind of fake urgency is manipulative at the best of times, but it’s especially concerning when the app is marketed toward people with ADHD, who are more vulnerable to impulse driven decisions.
If the developers really believed in their product, they’d let users test it properly before locking them into a year long payment. Until then, I’d strongly advise not giving this company your money.
author: Catata fish

title: AI Slop
body:
This is just chatGPT in a different outfit. After being charged $95 AUD to access it all I was given was a chatbot that gave inconsistent responses and didn’t provide any sound advice.
Have requested a refund of my money.
author: IsobelJo

title: Just Download Chat GPT
body: I should have known that with no free trial that this app would not be worth it. All this app is, is a list of pre designed questions and it  doesn’t like when you deviate from their order. If a question doesn’t align with your problem, the app just asks you the same question again. Is doesn’t feel like a conversation, it just feels like the app it talking at you. And the advice is so generic you could just google it.
author: Paytonlainey

title: Yet another ‘free to download’ app that charges to be used at all
body:
I was really excited by the marketing for this app. After doing about 15-30 mins of survey questions about my issues and goals, I get to the end only to see it requires either $30 per month or one outright yearly fee of $200 (marketed of course as a wonderful discount).
This reduces the appeal of the much-quoted “cancel anytime” statement because of course they don’t mind if you cancel. They’ve already got hundreds of your dollars. And for a system that makes such exorbitant promises (which I was very excited to put to the test) I find it very disconcerting that they do not have enough faith in their product to offer a lower tier or free trial - even for a couple days. Very disconcerting- these practices always seem scammy to me, so a fair warning to you all before you let an app psychoanalyse you for 20 minutes only to demand exorbitant funds before you see any results or have any actual idea of how this ‘magical revolutionary adhd cure’ app works. Also they spelt distractions wrong in their introduction. A pretty poor oversight for a service that values itself so highly, don’t you think?
author: Gencraneee
